nodes.text: For $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ let $f_r(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n=a_1+\cdots+a_r$ with $a_i\in A$. Does there exist, for all $r\geq 2$, a basis $A$ of order $r$ (so that $f_r(n)>0$ for all large $n$) such that\[\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x\]for all $x$?

#1192 : [Er80,p.99] additive combinatorics | additive basis Erdős and Rényi proved by the probabilistic method that there exists a set $A$ such that\[\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x\]and\[\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert\gg x^{1/r}\]for all $x$. Ruzsa [Ru90] proved that the answer is yes for $r=2$.
